subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: What can I now direct on my own, and what still needs someone else?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of assembling periodization, specialization, and leadership evidence in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe self-assessment against LEVEL 2 expectations using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply evaluating the cycle honestly, including what failed in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving identifying remaining dependencies on adult direction; correct it and explain why.
Connect setting the Grade 12 independence goal with defending design choices under questioning and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Present the LEVEL 2 portfolio to one trusted adult, defend the design choices in the training cycle and the facilitated session, and revise the Grade 12 plan after critique.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
